title: Craft Beer 6-pack

drivers.name: Supply risk: short delivery
drivers.evidence: Planner note warns of short delivery; no past occurrence, so noise-adjusted effect shrunk. Expected to suppress demand if stock is constrained.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 140.8. Thanksgiving (event week) has historically reduced demand by 7-13% (x0.87–0.98), but the noise-adjusted estimate is x1.0—indicating no reliable lift or decline. Price is unchanged (12.21), so no price effect. The planner note cites a short delivery, a supply risk that could limit availability and suppress sales. This is a credible downside driver with no historical precedent, so we apply a downward adjustment. Evidence is thin (one note), so shrink toward 1.0. The classical model suggests no uplift, which aligns with the noise-adjusted holiday effect. We adjust downward slightly for supply risk. No promotion, price change, or seasonality beyond the baseline. The baseline’s uncertainty is already calibrated.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-37% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
